notes: Dev-split RBox revision, following the geography template (twinned_with made asymmetric): it flips a property that holds (marriage is mutual) to its opposite. This edit counts as the topic's symmetry RBox edit. CRITERIA Rule 12 lists asymmetry under 'Not used anywhere'; we read that as applying to derivations of queries (an asymmetry question's 'no' is usually the same before and after), not to an RBox edit that removes symmetry, whose instance answers do change. Recorded here as an exception for the user to confirm. spouse_of is not the subject of any main-split RBox edit; its symmetry follows from no other tag (its other tag is functional), so there is no premise route back. The instances are true but minor couples (the chemists Ida and Walter Noddack, the mathematicians Hilda Geiringer and Richard von Mises), so a model is unlikely to hold the converse as a separate famous fact that competes with the edited property; famous couples were avoided. Both instance facts are in the past tense because both couples are dead; the direct question names the relation in the present, as the catalogue does. Yes and no are balanced through phrasing: the direct question asks 'asymmetric' (no, then yes), the first instance asks whether the converse follows (yes, then no), the second asks whether the negated converse follows (no, then yes), in the same plain 'Does it follow' form (it replaced 'Does that rule out', which small models may misread). The cross-lingual queries ask the first instance. Chinese marriage verbs are directed (嫁 for the bride, 娶 for the groom), so the zh prompt uses the neutral 与……结婚 in both sentences; an earlier parenthetical naming the wife was removed after review, since 'she is his wife' already states the converse. Names stay in Latin script. hops counts the instance fact as the bridge, as the other RBox records do.
